questions.question: What is the minimum size of grounding conductor required where a field-assembled grounding electrode is used as the grounding means for the following services: a) 150 A, service conductor 1/0 RW75; b) 400 A, 600 kcmil R90; c) 250 A, 350 kcmil TW (60°C); d) 500 A, 750 kcmil R90?
questions.answer: a) #4 (confirmed); b) c) d) require the full Table 43 bands above 200 A — see steps
solution_steps: Correct method (per class notes): the grounding conductor to a field-assembled electrode is sized from Table 43, keyed to the AMPACITY OF THE LARGEST SERVICE CONDUCTOR — NOT the breaker rating and NOT the load current. The earlier 'Table 17' reference was wrong; electrode sizing is Table 43 (bonding is Table 16).

Service conductors are taken at their rating temperature (75 °C for buildings; a 60 °C-rated cable such as TW is read in the 60 °C column). First get the conductor's ampacity from Table 2, then enter Table 43.
Table 43 documented bands: ampacity ≤ 165 A → size 4; 166–200 A → size 3; above 200 A the table continues 2, 1, 1/0, 2/0, 3/0 (worked example from notes: 4/0 Cu at 75 °C = 230 A → size 2).
a) 1/0 RW75 (75 °C) = 150 A ampacity → ≤ 165 A → grounding conductor size 4. CONFIRMED.

b) 600 kcmil R90 taken at 75 °C (≈ 420 A), c) 350 kcmil TW at 60 °C (≈ 250 A), d) 750 kcmil R90 at 75 °C (≈ 475 A) all fall above 200 A, where the exact Table 43 breakpoints are not documented in the class notes.
Keep needs_review: part (a) is resolved (#4) by the correct Table 43 / service-conductor-ampacity method; parts (b)(c)(d) need the printed CEC 2024 Table 43 bands above 200 A to confirm their sizes.

questions.question: The minimum spacing required between the two grounding electrodes installed in an electrical service is ........ m.
solution_steps: Rule 10-104: where a grounding electrode consists of two or more rod/plate electrodes, they must be spaced not less than 3 m apart so their earth-resistance spheres do not overlap.
Result: 3 m.

questions.question: Could a bare system grounding conductor be run together with the other system conductors in a 15 m length of conduit that contains one 90° and three 45° bends?
questions.answer: Yes — a 15 m run with 225° of bends is within both limits (≤15 m and ≤360° / four quarter-bends), so a bare system grounding conductor may share the raceway.
solution_steps: Rule 10-806: a bare (non-insulated) system grounding conductor is permitted in the same raceway as the system conductors where the run does not exceed 15 m (see S10-014).
Rule 12-940: total bends between pull points must not exceed 360° (four quarter-bends). One 90° + three 45° = 90° + 135° = 225°, which is less than 360°.
Both conditions are met: 15 m = the limit and 225° < 360°. The original 'two 90° bends' premise is not a CEC limit; the governing bend limit is 360°.
Result: Yes — permitted.

questions.question: The size of an equipotential bonding conductor must not be less than ........ if aluminum and ........ if copper.
questions.answer: #4 AWG if aluminum and #6 AWG if copper
solution_steps: Rule 10-406 (equipotential bonding) sets the minimum continuous bonding conductor size for equipotential bonding.
Minimum: #6 AWG copper, or #4 AWG aluminum (aluminum is one size larger to match copper conductance).
Result: #4 (Al), #6 (Cu).

questions.question: A field-assembled grounding electrode shall consist of a bare copper conductor of length ........ m.
solution_steps: Rule 10-102: a field-assembled (concrete-encased) grounding electrode consists of at least 6 m of bare copper conductor (not smaller than #4 AWG).
Result: 6 m.

questions.question: A field-assembled grounding electrode should be encased within the bottom ........ mm of a concrete foundation footing in direct contact with earth at not less than ........ mm below finished grade.
questions.answer: 50 mm of concrete; not less than 600 mm below finished grade
solution_steps: Rule 10-102: the bare copper conductor is encased within the bottom 50 mm of a concrete foundation footing that is in direct contact with earth.
The footing must be located not less than 600 mm below finished grade.
Result: 50 mm; 600 mm.

questions.question: What minimum size field-assembled copper grounding electrode would be required for a 100 A consumer service fed with #3 R90 copper conductors in a raceway?
solution_steps: Electrode-conductor sizing is by Table 43, keyed to the AMPACITY OF THE SERVICE CONDUCTOR (not the breaker, not the load). The earlier 'Table 17' reference was wrong.
Service conductor = #3 R90 copper, taken at 75 °C for a building (Table 2): #3 Cu at 75 °C = 110 A.
Enter Table 43 with 110 A: it falls in the lowest band (ampacity ≤ 165 A → size 4).
Result: #4 AWG copper. (The stated '#2 AWG' was an error from the wrong table; the 100 A / #3 service maps to the ≤ 165 A band → size 4.)

questions.question: What is the smallest size copper ground wire connected to a manufactured grounding electrode required for a 200 A residential consumer service fed with #3/0 R90 copper conductors?
solution_steps: Rule 10-114: the grounding conductor run to a manufactured (rod/plate) grounding electrode need not be larger than #6 Cu, regardless of service size.
So for the 200 A / #3/0 Cu service, the grounding conductor to a manufactured electrode is #6 Cu (the capped maximum applies).
Result: #6 AWG copper.

questions.question: A branch circuit is protected with a 40 A circuit breaker using No. 8 T90 copper conductors. What minimum size field-installed copper bonding conductor would be used if one were required in the raceway?
solution_steps: Rule 10-614/10-616: a bonding conductor is sized from the rating of the overcurrent device ahead of it, using Table 16 (ampere rating of OCPD → minimum copper bond).
Table 16: a 40 A overcurrent device requires a #10 Cu bonding conductor.
Result: #10 AWG copper. (The #8 T90 circuit conductors are not what sizes the bond — the 40 A device is.)

questions.question: On a photovoltaic DC supply circuit, what is required to be grounded in a two-wire system?
solution_steps: PV DC system grounding is governed by Section 64, not Section 10 — this question is mis-filed in the Section 10 set.
For a solidly-grounded 2-wire PV DC circuit, one conductor is grounded (option B).
Keep needs_review: CEC 2024 Section 64 widely permits functionally-grounded/ungrounded PV arrays, so the correct answer depends on the array type stated; verify against the specific Section 64 rule.

questions.question: A conductive metal raised floor in a computer room is to be bonded to ground. What is the minimum size of aluminum conductor required?
solution_steps: A conductive metal raised floor in a computer/data-processing room (Section 84) is bonded as equipotential bonding per Rule 10-406.
Minimum bonding conductor: #6 AWG aluminum (equivalent to #8 AWG copper — see S10-013).
Result: No. 6 AWG aluminum (option B).

questions.question: On a photovoltaic DC supply circuit, what is required to be grounded in a 2-wire system?
solution_steps: Duplicate of S10-010 (PV DC 2-wire grounding). Governed by Section 64, not Section 10.
For a solidly-grounded 2-wire PV DC circuit, one conductor is grounded (option B).
Keep needs_review: CEC 2024 Section 64 widely permits functionally-grounded/ungrounded PV arrays; verify against the specific Section 64 rule.

questions.question: A conductive metal raised floor in a computer room is to be bonded to ground. What is the minimum size of copper conductor required?
solution_steps: Conductive raised floor (Section 84) bonded as equipotential bonding per Rule 10-406.
Minimum copper bonding conductor is #8 AWG, corresponding to the #6 AWG aluminum minimum in S10-011.
Result: #8 AWG copper (option B).

questions.question: A non-insulated grounding conductor is being run in the same raceway with other insulated conductors. What is the maximum length of the conduit run?
solution_steps: Rule 10-806: a non-insulated (bare) grounding conductor may share a raceway with insulated conductors only where the raceway run does not exceed 15 m.
Result: 15 m (option B).
